title: helm(private): stabilize private values schema and init job templating for upgrade/rollback
author: Lena Park
description: Motivation: several clusters hit failures during Private upgrades due to tightened values.schema.json validation and an init job template that assumed nodeSelector/tolerations were present. This PR tightens the values schema to make encryption/kms/toleration fields explicit, makes templating defensive for optional nodeAffinity/nodeSelector/tolerations, and fixes an init-job race during upgrade/rollback. The description below covers the change summary, testing, upgrade notes and rollback strategy. Changes: 1) values.schema.json: add stricter types for .private.kms and .private.encryption options, mark some keys as required only when enableEncryption=true, document allowed provider enum (aws,kms,gcp,none). 2) templates/init-job.yaml: guard nodeSelector/tolerations blocks with has/and template helpers and fall back to empty maps to avoid YAML parsing errors on clusters without those fields. 3) templates/_helpers.tpl: add helper template 'redwood.private.nodeConstraints' used across charts to keep logic consistent. 4) Chart.yaml and readme/docs updated. 5) add scripts/helm/validate-values.sh to run schema validation in CI and local dev. Rollout plan: staged merge to main, ship next patch release for private installer, notify SRE and CSE teams with upgrade notes. Rollback: chart keeps old defaults, the init-job template now tolerates missing fields so rollback should not introduce previously observed failure modes. Checklist: - [x] values schema and docs updated - [x] guarded templating for init jobs - [x] unit tests for helper templates - [x] helm lint and template dry-run in CI - [x] upgrade tested against 2 internal clusters - [x] added migration notes in docs. Ticket references: ENG-9123 (upgrade failures), ENG-9187 (schema tightening).

This is a non-breaking change for clusters not enabling encryption.
